If you are looking to purchase a genuine antique Bible, `several reputable dealers and marketplaces specialize in historical, Reformation-era, and early American editions`.

### Where to Buy Antique Bibles

- **[Antique Bible Co.](https://www.antiquebible.com/):** A premier specialist run by collectors since 2006, focusing heavily on English Bibles prior to 1700 AD (including Geneva Bibles and early King James editions), as well as individual antique Bible leaves starting under $100. You can browse their active inventory on the [Antique Bible Shop](https://www.antiquebible.com/shop).[[1]](https://www.antiquebible.com/)[[2]](https://www.antiquebible.com/shop)
- **AbeBooks & Biblio:** Online marketplaces that aggregate rare, antiquarian, and out-of-print books from independent rare-book dealers worldwide. Searching for terms like *"1611 King James"* or *"16th century Bible"* yields verified dealer listings.
- **Sotheby’s & Christie’s / Major Auction Houses:** Best if you are searching museum-grade or investment-level artifacts (such as early leaves of the Gutenberg Bible or 15th/16th-century illuminated manuscripts).
- **Local Antiquarian Bookshops:** Visiting a brick-and-mortar rare book dealer allows you to inspect fragile rag-paper leaves, hand-tooled leather bindings, and brass clasps in person.

### What to Look For (and Expect on Price)

- **Age & Rarity:** 
	- 19th-century Victorian family Bibles (common) often sell anywhere from **$50 to $300** depending on condition and family history records inside.
	- 17th-century King James or Geneva Bibles typically range from **$3,000 to $20,000+**.
	- 16th-century Reformation prints (Tyndale, Great Bibles, or early Geneva printings) frequently command **$10,000 to $60,000+**.[[1]](https://www.antiquebible.com/shop)
- **Completeness:** Check whether the title page, maps, and genealogical tables are original or facsimile replacements. A missing title page can significantly impact value.
- **Condition of Bindings & Pages:** Original contemporary leather over oak boards, raised spine bands, metal cornerpieces, and edge-paintings add considerable value, whereas modern rebound covers will lower collector valuation.
- **Single Leaves:** If owning an entire 400-year-old volume is out of budget, buying an individual Antique Bible Leaf (a single page from a 1500s or 1600s Bible) is a popular and affordable entry point (often $75–$150).[[1]](https://www.antiquebible.com/)

Are you looking for a **specific era or translation** (e.g., a Victorian family Bible, a 17th-century King James, or an individual leaf), or do you have a **budget range** in mind?
